subject: [RFC PATCH 0/1] mm/swap: keep reclaim batches contiguous on swap

reviews.author: Kairui Song
reviews.summary: Reviewer Kairui Song suggested reverting commit 9a42aed48421, which prefers nonfull over free clusters for small order allocations, and instead always scanning full clusters to prioritize contiguity on large physical swap devices.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Alexandre,

That's a interesting problem. I think the real problem is with commit
9a42aed48421 ("mm, swap: prefer nonfull over free clusters"), right?

It's more like a balance between fragmentation and contiguity of small
order allocation issue.

Perhaps we should instead always scan the full clusters and revert
that one commit? That commit was only following the idea of keeping
the allocation more compacted for that series, it looked good at that
time. Since fragmentation issues can be solved in other ways,
contiguity seems to matter more for large physical swap devices.

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a reclaim batch spans multiple non-full clusters, which can lead to scattered writes and readahead requests.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti expressed interest in the proposed solution and asked for more information about alternative fragmentation solutions.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Kairui,

On Thu, Oct 22, 2026 at 5:27 PM Kairui Song <ryncsn@gmail.com> wrote:

---

Oh, okay. I thought reverting it wasn't an option given the good
numbers the patch provides.

What are the other fragmentation solutions you are referring to?

Thanks,

Alex

reviews.author: Nhat Pham
reviews.summary: Reviewer Nhat Pham expressed concerns that the proposed solution of allocating contiguous swap slots may not address the underlying issue and could lead to increased memory overhead, scanning overhead, etc., suggesting that physical swap space compaction is still a problem and virtual swap space would just shift the issue.
reviews.raw_body:
Hmm what other way are you thinking of? Physical swap space compaction
requires vswap, which has not landed. And we'd just be kicking the
problem to virtual swap space. Sure, we won't be failing allocation,
but that would still increase the memory overhead, scanning overhead,
etc.

I encountered this myself. Remember when I wrote my own swap allocator
for vswap? In one of the version, I went for free clusters first
instead of partial clusters. It fragmented the swap space, so I had to
copy your homework and went for partially used clusters first...

Anyway, maybe I'm wrong - some numbers would be nice here.

2026-10-22.patch_summary: This patch aims to reduce the number of I/O requests on a swap device by keeping reclaim batches contiguous. The current implementation of swap allocation and deallocation can lead to scattered writes, resulting in increased I/O requests. The patch modifies the allocator to allocate contiguous free slots for a reclaim batch, reducing the number of small requests and improving throughput. This is achieved by informing the allocator about the size of the batch and allowing it to allocate contiguous slots accordingly. The goal is to reduce the overhead of swap I/O operations and improve system performance.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Nhat Pham expressed support for the patch, noting that there are still workloads that benefit more from disk swapping than compression swapping, and requested that the swap subsystem be made to work for them.

The reviewer agrees with the patch's approach of allocating contiguous swap slots, noting that it makes sense to not apply the heuristic for large folios.

Reviewer Nhat Pham noted that the patch's approach of preferring non-full clusters over free clusters may lead to increased lock contention and fragmentation in swap files, but believes it will be fine as long as contiguity is found for the first time in the batch.

Reviewer Nhat Pham questioned the effectiveness of the patch's approach, noting that it may constantly overshoot the estimate of pages to be reclaimed due to rotating/promoting references, which could create problems down the line. He suggested collecting a batch of pages after unmapping and passing them to the phys swap allocator as an alternative solution.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks for looking into this! There are still workloads that benefit
more from disk swapping than compression swapping... We should make
the swap subsystem work for them.

I haven't read the code too closely, as it's an RFC meant to show the
general idea. So I'll just make some comments and ask some questions
about the idea:

---

Ah so we don't invoke this heuristics for folio larger than certain
orders? Makes sense.

---

So we prefer non-full clusters with contiguous slots, over free
clusters, over other nonfull clusters.

I think this part makes sense to me FWIW. We do skip fast path and go
for slow paths more often, so do make sure we're not paying with too
much lock contention, especially as the swapfile fils or get more
fragmented (which this patch series does nudge us towards). But FWIW,
we pretty much go back to the old behavior the moment we fail to find
contiguity for the first time in the batch, so I think we'll be
fine...?

---

Some general questions:

1. How many pages in folio_list typically do get reclaimed? There can
be quite a few with references, which we rotate/promote, when we scan,
right? Would constantly overshooting the estimate create problem down
the line?

(This is one of the few places where indirection (vswap) would have
helped - we can collect a batch of pages after unmapping, then pass
them to the phys swap allocator (after checking zswappability, etc.).
Maybe we can solve it better after it's landed, and accept an
imperfect solution for now?)

2. Should we skip this heuristics for cgroups that enables zswap (and
maybe zram)? Contiguity matters less there... unless it help at
writeback time? Hard to say without experimentation - maybe you can do
the same check you did for your zswap writeback batching patch series?

reviews.author: Kairui Song
reviews.summary:
Reviewer suggested limiting the patch's scope to SYNC devices or exploring simpler solutions to address the problem, expressing skepticism about the significance of a 4% reduction in mTHP failures.

Reviewer Kairui Song suggested addressing swap space fragmentation by sorting clusters by slot size before moving them back to the non-full list, which would mitigate the issue until a more comprehensive solution is implemented.
reviews.raw_body:
That patch is 1/3 of a series, that series yields really nice
results, but that one patch plays only a small part in them. Or
perhaps we can limit that to SYNC devices? I hope there are simpler
ways to avoid the problem you encountered. I think the ~4% reduction
of 64k mTHP failure is kind of trivial compared to the problem you
encountered, and 2M swapout is still not easily doable, as the
main blocker is from the page allocator.

---

Right, nothing has landed in upstream for that yet, but with larger
swap space the fragmentation issue will be largely solved. And before
that we might be able to sort the clusters by the continues size of
slots on it instead just blindly move then back to nonfull on any
freeing.

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a reclaim batch spans multiple non-full clusters, which could lead to fragmentation and inefficient allocation of swap slots.

Reviewer expressed concern that the patch might not benefit zswap with writeback enabled, specifically asking if it's intended to work on synchronous I/O devices

Reviewer noted that the current patch allocates swap slots per folio, not per batch, making sorting ineffective for this approach. They suggest implementing a sorting idea on top of this patch or reverting to nonfull cluster first allocation, and propose filling holes before allocating new clusters as the best solution.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Kairui,

Back from holidays, sorry for the late answer.

On Mon, Oct 26, 2026 at 2:38 PM Kairui Song <ryncsn@gmail.com> wrote:

---

I'm a bit scared it would not help zswap with writeback on, unless you
mean actual SWP_SYNCHRONOUS_IO devices?

---

Sorting would only help the current patch since reclaim allocates swap
slots per folio, not per batch.

What do you think the next move should be? Should we implement your
sorting idea on top of this patch or revert the nonfull cluster first
allocation? IMO, trying to fill the holes before allocating a new
cluster is the best solution. Doing that in reclaim, as I do here
avoids distinguishing between sync/async devices, so I'd favor a v2.

Let me know what you think and I'd go with your preferred idea,

Alex

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a reclaim batch spans multiple swap devices, which could lead to non-contiguous allocation of swap slots.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti noted that the patch description could be improved by explicitly mentioning that it addresses the issue of 'packing' large folios and suggested adding this detail to the changelog.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti expressed neutral sentiment and requested further investigation on the patch's impact, specifically asking to check its effect on zswap + writeback.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Nhat,

On Fri, Oct 23, 2026 at 6:05 PM Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com> wrote:

---

Yes, large folio get their own allocation scheme, here the idea is to
"pack" small folios, I'll add that to the changelog.

---

I was wondering the same, I'll check how it impacts zswap + writeback.

Thanks!

Alex

reviews.author: Kairui Song
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested scanning non-full clusters first for devices with synchronous I/O, and using free clusters first for other devices to maintain continuous IO patterns.
reviews.raw_body:
I mean maybe we can just scan nonfull first for SWP_SYNCHRONOUS_IO
devices? These devices are less sensitive to discretely distributed
I/O. For other devices we then prefer to keep the IO pattern
continuous by using free clusters first.

That may just fix the issue you are facing?

Or maybe some threshold or quick scan in partial_free_cluster before
putting the cluster back to nonfull.?
